comparison: Perfect agreement on electrophysiology claims (C21-C35). Both evaluations find the negative evidence well-supported across multiple experimental systems (HEK293, CHO, P1KO cells, reconstituted liposomes). Both rate as SUPPORTED and note these data challenge the mechanosensitive channel hypothesis.

Strong agreement on structural determination quality and dimeric architecture (C4-C6, C36-C40, C90-C91). Both evaluations find the cryo-EM structure well-supported. Peer review also includes detailed structural features (C7, C42-C45) that OpenEval addresses separately in R3. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R3 focuses on detailed structural features (C7, C42-C57) including dimerization interfaces and arrowhead shape. Peer R2 accepts these structural details as part of overall high-quality structural determination. Both rate as SUPPORTED, though peer review groups these with basic structural claims.

OpenEval R3 describes detailed dimerization interfaces (C49-C57). Peer R9 accepts the dimer formation and interface analysis as well-supported. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides more extensive structural detail while peer review accepts this as part of the overall structural quality.

Significant disagreement on absence of ion conduction pathway (C8, C47-C48, C59). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on structural evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting more thorough analysis of whether intracellular cavity could permit ion entry or whether alternative conformations might exist.

Strong agreement on CoA binding evidence (C10, C41, C71-C80). Both evaluations find the structural, biochemical, and mass spectrometry data well-supported. OpenEval notes both CoA and acetyl-CoA presence with CoA predominant. Both rate as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Perfect agreement on structural similarity to ELOVL7 (C11, C23, C60, C64-C65, C81-C82). Both evaluations find the computational structural comparisons well-supported using DALI and HHpred methods. Both rate as SUPPORTED and accept this as key evidence for alternative function.

Agreement on conserved histidine motif (C66-C68, C84). Both evaluations accept this as part of strong evidence for ELOVL similarity. OpenEval notes functional significance remains to be validated experimentally. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Agreement on parallel CoA binding capabilities between TMEM120A and ELOVL7 (C69-C70, C83). Both evaluations accept this as supporting functional similarity. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on lipid metabolism function hypothesis (C12, C85-C86). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this is speculation without direct enzymatic assays. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting this as a major implication. OpenEval emphasizes need for functional validation while peer reviewers accept the inference from structural similarity.

Agreement on uncertainty about membrane topology and localization (C46, C88-C89). Both evaluations accept the authors' acknowledgment of limitations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN and calls for experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty.

Agreement on background claims about prior TMEM120A research (C13-C20). Both evaluations accept these as accurate citations of previous literature. OpenEval notes these establish context for the controversy. Peer review specifically notes consistency with knockout mouse literature. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on basic descriptive claims (C1-C3). Both evaluations accept these as accurate background establishing TMEM120A as a transmembrane protein. Both rate as SUPPORTED as part of literature context.
Perfect agreement on ELOVL background claims (C24-C27, C61-C63). Both evaluations accept these as established facts from cited literature providing necessary context. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on obligate dimerization inference (C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on extensive structural interfaces but notes functional studies needed. Peer review accepts dimer formation as part of well-supported structural conclusions. Both find the structural evidence convincing.
